content: Vata is characterized by the elements of Air and Ether. It governs movement in the body, including breathing, muscle contraction, and heartbeat. Imbalance can lead to anxiety, dry skin, and constipation. Remedies include warm, oily foods and calming routine.

Pitta is associated with Fire and Water. It governs metabolism, digestion, and body temperature. Symptoms of imbalance include inflammation, anger, and acid reflux. Cooling foods like cucumber and coconut are recommended.

Kapha consists of Earth and Water. It provides structure, stability, and lubrication. Imbalance manifests as weight gain, lethargy, and sinus congestion. Stimulating activities and light, spicy foods help balance Kapha.

Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) is a powerful adaptogen. It helps the body manage stress, improves energy levels, and supports reproductive health. It is typically consumed as a powder mixed with warm milk or as a supplement.

Triphala is a combination of three fruits: Amla (Amalaki), Bibhitaki, and Haritaki. It is primarily used for digestive health, detoxification, and as a mild laxative. It is rich in vitamin C and antioxidants.

Ayurveda views indigestion (Ajirna) as a result of weak digestive fire (Agni). Drinking warm ginger water, avoiding cold drinks with meals, and consuming fennel seeds after eating can help improve digestion.
Joint pain is often linked to Vata accumulation. Local application of warm sesame oil or Mahanarayan oil, along with anti-inflammatory herbs like Turmeric and Shallaki, can provide relief.
